newsitem.title: USA: White House contradicts FBI on statement.
newsitem.headline: White House contradicts FBI on statement.

text.p: The White House publicly contradicted the FBI on Monday, saying there was an error in a statement the agency issued about its role in warning the White House that China might try to funnel money into the U.S. election campaign.

At issue is whether the FBI agents who made the warning last year asked two White House officials not to pass it up the chain of command to President Bill Clinton. The FBI statement said the agency made no such request; White House spokesman Mike McCurry contradicted that account and said the FBI statement was "in error."

"The White House legal counsel had very specific conversations with the two (White House) staffers in question. And they are adamant in recalling specifically that they were urged (by the FBI) not to disseminate the information outside the briefing room," McCurry said.

"Therefore the White House considers the FBI statement to be in error," said McCurry, who had come into the White House briefing room to make his remarks. Asked whether Clinton still has faith in FBI director Louis Freeh after the highly unusual public dispute, McCurry said, "Yes" but added, "I'm not going to go into it."

Clinton said earlier on Monday he was kept in the dark about an FBI warning last year that China might try to funnel money into the U.S. election campaign, and McCurry had told reporters that the FBI agents who briefed two White House officials about it last June had asked them not to tell higher-ups.

But the FBI statement said it "placed no restriction whatsoever on the dissemination up the chain-of-command at the NSC on any information" provided at the June briefing. The FBI said the briefing concerned "possible covert activities of a foreign government in the United States," but gave no further details.
